This proof relies on reducing to positive characteristic and utilizes the non-abelian Hodge correspondence in characteristic p linking Dolbeault and de Rham moduli spaces.

Pre-trained language models have significantly enhanced performance across numerous natural language processing tasks. While most state-of-the-art models focus on individual aspects such as data processing, pre-training objectives, neural architecture, or fine-tuning strategies, this paper investigates the impact of these approaches in isolation and demonstrates that optimal results on a specific question-answering task are achieved when these methods are integrated during pre-training. Specifically, we introduce an extended pre-training objective and a novel neighbor-aware mechanism designed to prioritize neighboring tokens, thereby enriching context representation. Our best-performing model achieves new state-of-the-art scores of 95.7% F1 and 90.6% EM on the SQuAD 1.1 dataset and surpasses existing models—including RoBERTa, ALBERT, ELECTRA, and XLNet—on the SQuAD 2.0 benchmark.

This work investigates the local analytical integrability near a $p:-q$ resonant singular point of a two-dimensional vector field, exploring its relationship with time-reversibility under the non-smooth involution $\varphi(x,y)=(y^{p/q},x^{q/p})$. Furthermore, it extends the theory originally formulated by K.~S.~Sibirsky for the $1:-1$ resonant scenario to the broader $p:-q$ resonant case.

We establish theoretical equivalences between stochastic and deterministic frameworks for age-stratified populations of individual cells. Specifically, we construct a hierarchical equation system that captures the complete dynamics of an age-structured multi-stage Markov process to approximate cell cycle time distributions. We further show that the resulting mean behavior aligns with the classical McKendrick-von Foerster integro-partial differential equation over large timescales. Finally, we extend this approach to a spatial setting, enabling the modeling of traveling waves and cell-mediated pattern formation. More broadly, this methodology can be applied to a wide range of reaction-diffusion processes where individual age significantly influences dynamics.

The inability of deep neural networks to generalize on out-of-distribution data is a recognized issue that creates significant concerns regarding their deployment in safety-critical sectors like healthcare, finance, and autonomous driving. This study examines a specific type of distribution shift: shortcuts or spurious correlations present in training data. Shortcut learning typically remains hidden until models are tested on real-world data lacking these same spurious patterns, creating a major challenge for AI practitioners in accurately evaluating a model's readiness for practical use. To address this, we propose utilizing mutual information (MI) between the learned representations and inputs as a metric to identify when and where a network relies on shortcuts during training. Experimental results indicate that MI serves as an effective, domain-agnostic tool for monitoring shortcut learning.

Normative modeling has emerged as a promising method for capturing individual variations in neuroimaging data to identify psychiatric biomarkers. While current implementations utilize Gaussian process regression to generate coherent uncertainty estimates, they face limitations such as inefficient scaling for large datasets and dependence on fixed parametric kernels. To address these issues, this paper introduces a deep normative modeling framework based on neural processes (NPs). We formulate a stochastic process approach for mixed-effect models, demonstrating how NPs can facilitate spatially structured mixed-effect modeling of neuroimaging data. This approach allows for the learning of optimal feature representations and covariance structures for random effects and noise through global latent variables, with predictive uncertainty approximated by sampling from these distributions. Evaluated on a publicly available clinical fMRI dataset, the proposed NP-based multivariate normative models significantly outperformed a baseline multi-task Gaussian process regression approach in novelty detection for specific diagnostic tasks.

In the domain of quality assurance for hybrid systems—which integrate continuous physical dynamics with discrete digital control—Platzer's differential dynamic logic (dL) is a prominent deductive verification approach, known for its rigorous mathematical basis and advanced tooling. Driven by benchmarks from an industry partner, we investigate a relational extension of dL to formally verify claims like "deploying the emergency brake earlier reduces collision speed." A primary technical hurdle involves correlating states across two distinct dynamics at separate time points. Our key contributions include a theory of appropriate simulations (a relational counterpart to differential invariants, which are core proof techniques in dL) and a derived method called time stretching. The latter offers high practical utility because it does not require users to manually construct simulations from scratch. Based on these concepts, we establish new inference rules for dL and validate them through several automotive case studies.

The [CII] $158\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ fine-structure line serves as a primary coolant for the neutral interstellar medium, making it one of the most luminous far-infrared emission lines detectable in star-forming regions across the Galaxy, as well as in the diffuse interstellar medium and distant galaxies. Although [CII] emission is often proposed as a robust indicator of star formation, this study aims to clarify its origins and its connection to other tracers of interstellar gas and dust. Specifically, we investigate gas heating efficiency using the [CII] line to evaluate existing heating models. Our analysis utilizes a one-square-degree, velocity-resolved map of [CII] emission toward the Orion Nebula complex, encompassing M43 and NGC 1977. We observe a strong correlation between [CII] intensity and PAH emission in the IRAC $8\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ band, as well as far-infrared radiation from warm dust. However, the relationship between [CII] and CO(2-1) varies depending on the region's detailed geometry. Notably, we identify particularly low [CII]-to-FIR intensity ratios in areas with large columns of both warm and cold dust, supporting an interpretation of the "[CII] deficit" as a "FIR excess." A minor reduction in the FIR line-to-continuum ratio is linked to diminished gas heating efficiency. Furthermore, at the spatial scales mapped, star-formation rates derived from [CII] emission in the Orion Nebula complex are roughly ten times lower than those calculated from young stellar object (YSO) counts. Finally, [CII] emission in this complex originates predominantly from cloud surfaces, many of which are viewed edge-on, suggesting that [CII] from extended, faint cloud surfaces may significantly contribute to total [CII] emission on galactic scales.

Precisely identifying the location of every individual in crowded scenes is a vital component of crowd analysis. Yet, conventional density-based approaches yield only coarse results, while segmentation or detection-based techniques struggle with highly dense environments and significant scale variations. To address these challenges, we introduce Independent Instance Map segmentation (IIM), an end-to-end and straightforward framework for crowd localization. Unlike density maps or bounding box regression, IIM ensures that each instance is non-overlapping. By partitioning crowds into independent connected components, the system simultaneously determines positions and counts (derived from component centers and quantities, respectively). Additionally, to enhance segmentation quality across varying density levels, we propose a Differentiable Binarization Module (BM) that generates structured instance maps. This module offers two key benefits: 1) it adaptively learns a threshold map tailored to different images for more accurate instance detection, and 2) it enables direct training using binary prediction losses. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our method is effective and surpasses state-of-the-art techniques on five prominent crowd datasets. Notably, IIM achieves a 10.4% improvement in F1-measure on the NWPU-Crowd Localization task. The source code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/taohan10200/IIM.

This study examines data-driven segmentation utilizing Re-Pair or Byte Pair Encoding techniques. Unlike prior research that mainly concentrated on subword units for machine translation, our focus lies on the general characteristics of segments operating above the word level, which we term r-grams. We analyze these r-grams' properties and their impact on token frequency distributions. The approach's viability is assessed through embedding techniques in both monolingual and multilingual contexts. Additionally, we present several qualitative examples that illustrate the method's effectiveness as a language-invariant segmentation procedure.

Existing Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) methods are limited to identifying a single primary unseen object category within an image. We posit that this constraint is inadequate for real-world scenarios where unseen objects typically appear as components of complex scenes, necessitating both the `recognition' and `localization' of novel categories. To address this gap, we propose a new \emph{`Zero-Shot Detection'} (ZSD) framework designed to simultaneously detect and localize instances of unseen categories without requiring training data. Additionally, we introduce a novel experimental protocol for ZSD utilizing the challenging ILSVRC dataset, which accounts for practical constraints such as the scarcity of unseen objects. To our knowledge, this represents the first end-to-end deep network for ZSD that jointly models the interaction between visual and semantic domain information. To mitigate noise inherent in automatically generated semantic descriptions, we employ the concept of meta-classes to create a unique loss function that harmonizes max-margin class separation with semantic space clustering. Furthermore, we present a baseline method adapted from recognition to the detection setting. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate a substantial performance improvement over the baseline on the critical and difficult ZSD task.

Finite frames, which serve as spanning sets for finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, are a fundamental tool in signal processing. Recent research has extensively explored the global structure of finite frames with specific properties, such as unit norm tight frames. This work generalizes those findings to the broader context of fusion frames—collections of subspaces within a finite-dimensional Hilbert space where any vector can be reconstructed from its projections. The concept of tightness is also extended to fusion frames, leading to the inquiry of whether the set of tight fusion frames with fixed subspace dimensions forms a path-connected space. We affirmatively answer this question (a generalized version of a result by Cahill, Mixon, and Strawn regarding unit norm tight frames). Furthermore, we extend the work of Benedetto and Fickus, who demonstrated that the frame potential on unit norm frames has no spurious local minimizers and that its global minimizers are tight, thereby allowing gradient descent to construct such frames. We prove an analogous result for the fusion frame potential defined by Casazza and Fickus: when tight fusion frames exist for a specific set of dimensions, they can be generated via gradient descent. Our proofs rely on techniques from symplectic geometry and Mumford's geometric invariant theory.

This paper establishes the Euler characteristics and signatures for exact symplectic fillings of contact double, 3-fold, and 4-fold cyclic covers of the standard contact 3-sphere that branch over specific transverse quasi-positive links. These links encompass all quasi-positive knots with crossing numbers below 11, as well as all quasi-positive links with crossing numbers below 12 and nonzero nullity.

Famous disputes between Klein and Einstein centered on whether General Relativity possesses physically significant conserved quantities. This paper examines the implications of Noether's second theorem for that debate, linking them to Einstein's pursuit of a "substantive" form of general covariance and his efforts to broaden the Principle of Relativity. We contend that Noether's second theorem offers a definitive method to differentiate between theories where gauge or diffeomorphism symmetry actively defines charges and those where such symmetry arises merely from Kretchmannization. Additionally, we discuss the connection between this Noetherian concept of substantive general covariance and the idea of "background independence."

We examine a hierarchy of nondeterminism comprising three distinct levels. First, a nondeterministic automaton $\cal A$ is considered determinizable by pruning (DBP) if removing certain transitions yields an equivalent deterministic automaton. Second, $\cal A$ is classified as good-for-games (GFG) if its nondeterministic choices can be resolved based solely on the history of inputs. Third, $\cal A$ is termed semantically deterministic (SD) when different nondeterministic choices lead to equivalent states. Although formal methods applications often require deterministic automata, they can effectively utilize automata with varying degrees of nondeterminism; specifically, DBP automata aid in analyzing online algorithms, while GFG automata are valuable for synthesis and control. While these three levels coincide for automata operating on finite words, we investigate their hierarchy for B\"uchi, co-B\"uchi, and weak automata on infinite words. Our findings demonstrate that the hierarchy is strict, and we analyze the expressive power of each level alongside the computational complexity of determining language membership. Furthermore, we present a probability-based analysis of the hierarchy, linking the degree of nondeterminism to the likelihood that a random accepting run exists for a word within the language.

The principal ratio of a graph is defined as the ratio between the largest and smallest components of its principal eigenvector. Because this metric relies on extreme values, it is highly sensitive to outliers, which can pose challenges for networks derived from empirical data. To address this issue, we examine the dispersion of both the principal eigenvector and the degree vector, specifically utilizing the coefficient of variation—the ratio of standard deviation to mean. We demonstrate that both statistics are bounded above by an identical function of the principal ratio, a bound that is tight for regular graphs. This paper aims to prove that the coefficient of variation for these vectors can converge to or diverge from the principal ratio in the limit. Through this analysis, we identify a specific family of graphs, the complete split graph, whose principal ratio converges to the golden ratio. Finally, we present conjectures regarding extremal graphs for these statistics and highlight notable properties of the complete split graph.

State estimation becomes essential when addressing high-dimensional dynamical systems, particularly because complete measurements are frequently inaccessible; it is fundamental for gaining insights, executing control strategies, and optimizing designs. However, most deep learning methods are limited by their reliance on high-resolution labels and fixed sensor configurations. Furthermore, applying Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) to sparse data presents significant challenges. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel approach utilizing an implicit optimization layer and a physics-informed loss function capable of learning from sparse labels. By minimizing the energy of the neural network's predictions, this technique accommodates varying sensor counts and locations. Building on this framework, we develop two models for discrete and continuous spatial predictions. We validate the models' efficacy on two high-dimensional fluid dynamics problems: the Burgers' equation and Flow Past a Cylinder for the discrete model, and the Allen-Cahn and Convection-diffusion equations for the continuous model. Additionally, we demonstrate that the proposed models maintain robustness against noisy measurements.

Policies serve as authoritative resources spanning multiple domains to facilitate decision-making by defining permitted or recommended actions when specific conditions regarding entities and their attributes are met. These policies frequently incorporate geographical constraints, such as distance and containment relations between named locations, whose polygonal boundaries are often encoded within geospatial datasets. This work introduces a method to convert data from such datasets into Linked Data using OWL, PROV-O, and GeoSPARQL standards, thereby enabling automated, ontology-driven policy decisions. We demonstrated this approach by analyzing location-sensitive radio spectrum policies to determine relationships between radio transmitter coordinates and policy-regulated regions found in Census.gov data. By employing an evaluation pipeline that integrates OWL reasoning with GeoSPARQL, our method successfully implements the necessary geospatial relationships in accordance with requirements defined by radio spectrum domain experts.

Uncertainty sampling is widely employed in active learning to minimize annotation expenses, yet there remains no broad agreement on the optimal uncertainty estimation function for binary classification, and the convergence properties of related algorithms are poorly understood; this challenge is compounded in multi-class scenarios. This study introduces an efficient uncertainty estimator for binary classification that is also adaptable to multiple classes, offering a non-asymptotic convergence rate for our uncertainty sampling-based active learning approach under both noise-free (linearly separable) and noisy conditions for both binary and multi-class tasks.

This study examines majority-logic decoding within reversible and finite-time information erasure processes applied to macroscopic bits composed of $N$ microscopic binary units. Although single-unit transformations prove more efficient for reversible erasure protocols, majority-logic decoding demonstrates significant advantages in finite-time scenarios: it reduces both the minimum erasure duration required for a specific erasure level and the minimum erasure error achievable within a fixed duration, outperforming single-unit approaches. Notably, this method remains superior in regimes characterized by both low erasure error and rapid erasure. These benefits persist even when employing the optimal erasure protocol designed to minimize dissipated heat. Consequently, our findings indicate that majority-logic decoding can overcome the precision-speed-efficiency trade-off inherent in information erasure processes.

An oracle serves as a mechanism to determine if the outputs of a program for executed test cases are correct; however, for machine learning programs, such an oracle is often unavailable or too difficult to implement. Metamorphic testing addresses this by utilizing metamorphic relations—essential properties of the software under test—to verify correctness. Prioritizing these relations can lower the costs associated with metamorphic testing [1]. Yet, prioritizing based on code coverage is frequently ineffective for machine learning programs because their decision logic is derived from training data, allowing 100% code coverage to be achieved with just a single test input. To address this, this work proposes a cost-effective method that prioritizes metamorphic relations for machine learning programs based on diversity in the source and follow-up datasets. We demonstrate that this data diversity-based approach improves fault detection effectiveness by up to 40% compared to code coverage-based methods and reduces the time required to detect faults by 29% compared to random execution of metamorphic relations. Consequently, our approach saves both time and cost during the testing phase.

BINGO (Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from Integrated Neutral Gas Observations) is a radio telescope engineered to survey frequencies between 980 MHz and 1260 MHz, targeting the neutral Hydrogen (HI) 21-cm line to detect the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) signal using Intensity Mapping. This paper introduces our methodology for generating mock maps of the 21-cm Intensity Mapping signal across the BINGO frequency band, along with associated validation results. (Abridged)

This study examines the maximal $B_{p,q}^{s}$-regularity properties of a nonlocal fractional elliptic equation. Specifically, it demonstrates that the operator associated with this nonlocal equation is sectorial within $B_{p,q}^{s}$ and serves as a generator for an analytic semigroup. Furthermore, the well-posedness of the corresponding nonlocal fractional parabolic equation in Besov spaces is established.

This work introduces and examines the concept of a multivalued $\lambda$-dissipative probability vector field (MPVF) within the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathsf X)$, where $\mathsf X$ is a Hilbert space containing Borel probability measures. Drawing upon dissipative operator theory in Hilbert spaces and the framework of Wasserstein gradient flows for geodesically convex functionals, we analyze both local and global well-posedness for evolution equations governed by dissipative MPVFs. Our methodology employs a measure-theoretic adaptation of the Explicit Euler scheme, yielding new convergence results with optimal error bounds under an abstract CFL stability condition; notably, these results avoid compactness arguments and remain valid even in infinite-dimensional settings $\mathsf X$. We define limit solutions via a specific Evolution Variational Inequality (EVI), modeled after the integral solutions to dissipative evolutions in Banach spaces proposed by B\'enilan. Subsequently, we establish the existence, uniqueness, and stability of these EVI solutions under broad assumptions, thereby generating a semigroup of nonlinear contractions.

A question is posed regarding whether every handle-irreducible summand of a stable-ribbon surface-link constitutes a unique ribbon surface-link; this is affirmatively resolved for the specific case of trivial surface-links. Specifically, any handle-irreducible summand of a stably trivial surface-link is shown to be merely a trivial 2-link. By integrating this finding with a previous result by F. Hosokawa and the author—which establishes that all surface-knots possessing an infinite cyclic fundamental group are stably trivial—it is deduced that every surface-knot with an infinite cyclic fundamental group is, in fact, a trivial (unknotted) surface-knot.

This study addresses the well-posedness of a subsonic, axially symmetric jet flowing from a semi-infinite nozzle onto a rigid boundary, governed by the steady isentropic Euler equations. We demonstrate that for a given mass flux below a critical threshold $M_{cr}$, a unique smooth subsonic jet exists that exits the nozzle and strikes an uneven wall. The jet's surface acts as a free boundary that smoothly detaches from the nozzle's edge. Furthermore, we established that a specific pressure difference between the chamber and the atmosphere ensures a continuous fit for this free boundary. Additionally, we derived the asymptotic behaviors and decay properties of the jet and its free surface in the downstream region. These findings resolve an open problem regarding the well-posedness of compressible, axially symmetric impinging jets originally posed by A. Friedman in Chapter 16 of [FA2]. Our proof primarily relies on a variational approach applied to quasilinear elliptic equations featuring Bernoulli-type free boundaries.

We investigate the electronic, magnetic, and thermodynamic characteristics of both ordered and chemically disordered FeRh alloys using ab-initio techniques, focusing on the equiatomic Fe$_{50}$Rh$_{50}$ composition for each phase. Additionally, we examine chemically disordered Fe$_x$Rh$_{100-x}$ systems to analyze how disorder influences their electronic and magnetic behaviors. The study also incorporates the effects of stress and strain within both ordered and disordered states, restricting results to the cubic phase without accounting for distortions. Driven by renewed interest in FeRh due to the potential for sustainable barocaloric cycles, this research explores the combined influence of chemical disorder and pressure on Fe$_x$Rh$_{100-x}$ to elucidate their synergistic effects and interactions.

This paper investigates enhancing the end-to-end data rates for ground users supported by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and tethered balloons (TBs), aiming to maximize network throughput in areas lacking terrestrial infrastructure. Initially, an integer linear programming approach is employed to optimize user associations. Next, the UAV transmission powers are determined optimally by transforming the problem into a convex form. Following this, an efficient algorithm is introduced to refine UAV positioning. Finally, the proposed mathematical framework is validated through selected numerical results that demonstrate the benefits of the suggested scheme.

Although existing literature on Machine Learning (ML) security primarily addresses unrealistic adversarial examples, recent studies have highlighted the need to explore realistic attacks and their impact on real-world system robustness. This paper advances the understanding of adversarial robustness against such realistic threats through two primary contributions. First, we evaluate the efficacy of unrealistic examples in defending against realistic ones across three real-world applications—text classification, botnet detection, and malware detection—using five datasets. Our findings reveal significant variations across these use cases, where unrealistic examples either perform comparably to realistic ones or provide only marginal improvements. Second, to elucidate these outcomes, we examine the latent representations of adversarial examples generated by both realistic and unrealistic attacks, identifying patterns that determine which unrealistic examples effectively harden models. We also open-source our code, datasets, and models to facilitate future research into bridging the gap between unrealistic and realistic adversarial attacks.

This research investigates the generalizability of Spike Timing Dependent Plasticity (STDP), an unsupervised, neuro-inspired learning technique used to train Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs). By examining the Hausdorff dimension of the algorithm's learning trajectories, the study evaluates how specific STDP models and their hyper-parameters influence generalizability. Furthermore, these insights are leveraged to formulate a Bayesian optimization strategy aimed at tuning STDP hyper-parameters to enhance the generalizability of SNNs.

We have previously established BRST quantization for a hypersurface $V_{N-1}$ embedded in $N$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}_N$ using both Hamiltonian and Lagrangian approaches. This work extends that formalism to an $L$-dimensional manifold $V_L$ embedded in $\mathbb{R}_N$, where $1 \leq L < N$. The resulting framework remains essentially consistent with our earlier findings. Furthermore, we have confirmed these results through a straightforward example involving particle dynamics on a torus knot.

Addressing complex real-world issues often demands the integration of diverse reasoning skills, including effective abstractions, commonsense knowledge, and the inventive combination of problem-solving tactics. To propel AI development toward these capabilities, we introduce a novel reasoning benchmark called Fermi Problems (FPs). These are inquiries where exact calculations are unfeasible or impossible, necessitating approximate estimates; a classic example is determining the global sea-level rise if all ice melted. While FPs have long been utilized in quizzes and interviews to assess human creative reasoning, we now apply this framework to AI by providing two datasets: a set of 1,000 real-world FPs drawn from competitions and quizzes, and a collection of 10,000 synthetic FPs of intermediate difficulty to act as a training sandbox. Beyond question-answer pairs, these resources include detailed, executable program solutions and supporting facts to facilitate the supervision and evaluation of intermediate reasoning steps. Our analysis reveals that even large language models subjected to extensive fine-tuning struggle significantly, with average estimates deviating by two orders of magnitude. Ultimately, this work consolidates several unresolved AI challenges into a unified benchmark designed to inspire progress in building more capable reasoning systems.

Noncoding RNAs play essential roles in diverse biological functions, such as translation, gene regulation, host-pathogen interactions, and environmental sensing. Although genomics has matured, identifying noncoding RNA elements in bacterial and archaeal genomes remains challenging due to the difficulties of *de novo* detection. While emerging technologies like RNA-seq have enhanced the identification and quantification of noncoding RNAs, a significant hurdle persists in distinguishing functional transcripts from transcriptional noise. To assess whether current transcriptome annotations capture all functional outputs, we analyzed over 400 public RNA-seq datasets covering 37 species of Bacteria and Archaea. Using comparative methods, we identified nearly 1,000 highly expressed candidate noncoding RNAs. However, our findings indicate that the ability to detect these outputs is heavily reliant on phylogenetic sampling. Surprisingly, unlike protein-coding genes, the phylogenetic window for effectively applying comparative tools is unexpectedly narrow; aggregating public data yielded only a single phylogenetic cluster where these methods could robustly separate unannotated noncoding RNAs from transcriptional noise. Our results demonstrate that to fully realize the potential of transcriptomics, experimental design must evolve: effective transcriptomics demands phylogeny-aware sampling.

Entity Linking involves identifying mentions within a text and matching them to entities in a specific knowledge base (KB), a process that aids in annotating vast amounts of web documents to extract new facts. However, current Entity Linking systems typically rely on models that are domain-specific and optimized for the particular KB used during training, leading to suboptimal performance when tested on documents or KBs from different domains. While pre-trained language model approaches, such as those by Wu et al. (2020), offer promise in zero-shot scenarios for general-domain KBs, they fail to match performance levels when applied to domain-specific KBs. To address this, we introduce Cross-Domain Neural Entity Linking (CDNEL), a framework designed to enable a single system to link entities simultaneously across both general and domain-specific KBs. CDNEL achieves this by learning a shared representation space that bridges different domains. We evaluate the method using the external Entity Linking dataset (Zeshel) by Logeswaran et al. (2019) and the Reddit dataset by Botzer et al. (2021), comparing our results against state-of-the-art benchmarks. By fine-tuning on various dataset types, we generate multiple CDNEL model variants. Testing these variants across four domains within the Zeshel dataset yields an average precision improvement of 9%.

This study introduces a noise estimation and subtraction algorithm designed to enhance the sensitivity of heterodyne laser interferometers by a factor of ten. Specifically, the interferometer is tailored for dynamic measurements of test masses within sub-Hz inertial sensing applications. After applying the proposed noise subtraction technique to a benchtop prototype—which initially exhibited a noise level of 2.76E-10 m/rtHz at 100mHz under vacuum conditions at 3E-5 Torr—the system achieved a significantly reduced noise floor of 3.31E-11 m/rtHz at the same frequency. Building on these findings, we examined noise mitigation strategies for non-linear optical pathlength noise, laser frequency noise, and temperature fluctuations inherent to heterodyne laser interferometers. For each identified noise source, we quantified its contribution and eliminated it from the data using either linear fitting or spectral analysis algorithms. The noise correction methodology presented herein is broadly applicable to heterodyne laser interferometers.

Since 1992, the Birmingham Solar-Oscillations Network (BiSON) has maintained its full complement of six stations. Looking back more than two decades later, this review examines the network's history by analyzing site metadata to evaluate performance regarding solar insolation and highlighting challenges faced over time. We also describe how the international community can readily access the network's expanding dataset and conclude by exploring the network's future, including the potential influence of nearly 25 years of technology miniaturization.

This study examines the connection between symmetries, conserved quantities, and the emergence of the boundary time crystal (BTC) phase within a generalized spin model featuring Lindblad dissipation. BTCs represent a non-equilibrium state of matter where a system interacting with an external environment breaks continuous time-translation invariance. Through a comprehensive mean-field analysis supported by finite-size scaling of a quantum $p,q$-spin interaction system—suitable for implementation in fully-connected spin-1/2 ensembles—we identify two critical conditions for observing the BTC phase. First, the discrete $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry inherent to the Hamiltonian must be explicitly broken by the Lindblad jump operators. Second, the system must couple uniformly to a single bath to maintain total angular momentum conservation throughout the time evolution. If either condition fails, any oscillatory behavior is merely transient, eventually settling into a time-independent stationary state. Our findings indicate that these two factors likely constitute general prerequisites for a stable BTC phase, linking symmetries and conserved quantities across arbitrary spin models.

We propose and investigate knowledge drift (KD), a sophisticated type of drift specific to hierarchical classification. In KD scenarios, the concept vocabulary, their individual distributions, and the hierarchical "is-a" relationships between them may all evolve over time. The primary difficulty arises because the true concept hierarchy remains unobserved, making it challenging to distinguish between various forms of KD. For example, the addition of a new "is-a" link between two concepts could be mistaken for individual changes to those concepts, despite being fundamentally different. Failing to correctly identify the specific type of KD undermines the classifier's hierarchy, resulting in systematic prediction errors. Our key insight is that in many human-in-the-loop systems, such as smart personal assistants, users are aware of recent drift occurrences and their nature. Leveraging this, we present TRCKD, a new method that integrates automated drift detection and adaptation with an interactive phase where users help disambiguate between different KD types. Furthermore, TRCKD employs a straightforward yet effective knowledge-aware adaptation strategy. Our simulations demonstrate that on both synthetic and real-world data, only a few queries to the user are often sufficient to significantly enhance prediction performance.

The codewords of the homomorphism code $\operatorname{aHom}(G,H)$ represent affine homomorphisms between two finite groups, $G$ and $H$, which extends the concept of Hadamard codes. Building upon prior research by Goldreich--Levin (1989), Grigorescu et al. (2006), Dinur et al. (2008), and Guo and Sudan (2014), we broaden the scope of groups admitting local list-decoding up to $\textsf{mindist}$, the code's minimum distance. Notably, we eliminate the previous necessity for either $G$ or $H$ to be solvable. Specifically, we establish a $\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$ bound on the list size—the count of codewords within distance $(\textsf{mindist}-\varepsilon)$ of any received word—when $G$ is either abelian or an alternating group, and $H$ is any arbitrary group (finite or infinite). We hypothesize that this bound applies to all finite simple groups as domains, with alternating groups serving as the initial proof of concept.

This result, distinguishing between abelian and arbitrary groups, allows us to adapt existing methods to achieve efficient local list-decoding for this scenario. Additionally, we derive efficient local list-decoding for the permutation representations of alternating groups (where the codomain is a symmetric group $S_m$), provided the domain $G=A_n$ and codomain $H=S_m$ satisfy the condition $m < 2^{n-1}/\sqrt{n}$. Restrictions on the codomain in this latter instance stem from significant technical challenges related to solving the homomorphism extension (HomExt) problem in specific contexts; these issues are resolved in a separate publication by Wuu (2018). Furthermore, we propose an intermediate "semi-algorithmic" framework termed Certificate List-Decoding, which circumvents the HomExt bottleneck within the alternating vs. arbitrary setting. A certificate list-decoder generates partial homomorphisms that uniquely determine the full homomorphisms comprising the list.

This paper presents a new proof of the Montejano and Karasev theorem concerning $k$-dimensional transversals for small collections of convex sets. Unlike their original approach, which relies on intricate algebraic and topological methods, our demonstration is a straightforward application of the Borsuk-Ulam theorem. Furthermore, in specific instances, our findings provide a stronger result than the theorem established by Montejano and Karasev.

In 2008, Bella, Olshevsky, and Prasad demonstrated that the Lipschitz stability of flipped orthogonal (FO) Jordan bases for H-selfadjoint matrices holds under small perturbations. Later, in 2022, Dogruer, Minenkova, and Olshevsky addressed the real case, introducing a more refined set of bases known as FOCS bases for real H-selfadjoint matrices; these bases feature both flipped orthogonality and the conjugate symmetric (CS) property. This paper establishes that these new FOCS bases are also Lipschitz stable under small perturbations, and it further proves the Lipschitz stability of the classical real canonical Jordan bases.

Astrometric data from S-stars offer a distinct means to investigate the characteristics of Sagittarius-A* (Sgr-A*). Consequently, understanding the dynamics of timelike bound trajectories around a massive central body has become crucial. It is established that while Schwarzschild black holes preclude negative precession for S-stars, naked singularity spacetimes permit both positive and negative precession in bound timelike orbits. In this study, we examine the perihelion precession of a test particle within Kerr spacetime geometry. Under specific approximations, we explore whether negative precession is possible for bound timelike orbits in Kerr spacetime, focusing exclusively on low-eccentricity equatorial orbits. Our findings indicate that negative precession for such bound timelike orbits is not permitted in Kerr spacetimes.

This paper examines the lattice of restricted subalgebras within a restricted Lie algebra. Specifically, it investigates algebras where this lattice is dually atomistic, semimodular (either lower or upper), or where every restricted subalgebra functions as a quasi-ideal. The existence of one-dimensional subalgebras that fail to be restricted causes several of these conditions to be less restrictive compared to their counterparts in the non-restricted context.

The spontaneous chemical cross-linking of monomers into hydrogels gives rise to a fractal structure, which has been directly associated with power-law viscoelasticity at the gel transition, as recently shown in isostatic (marginally rigid) spring networks modeled after the Sierpinski triangle. In this work, we extend the generation rules of the Sierpinski triangle to create four distinct fractals, all sharing the same dimension $d_{\rm f}=\log 3/\log 2$, with the original Sierpinski triangle representing just one instance. We demonstrate that spring networks constructed from these fractals remain isostatic yet display one of two different exponents for their power-law viscoelasticity. Consequently, we conclude that for networks with fixed connectivity, power-law viscoelasticity cannot be determined solely by the fractal dimension.

The High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) is designed to achieve a peak luminosity of $5\times10^{34}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, representing a five-fold increase over the original LHC design. The ATLAS Tile Calorimeter (TileCal), a hadronic sampling detector utilizing steel absorbers and plastic scintillators, currently guides light from the tiles to photomultiplier tubes (PMTs). These tubes generate analogue signals that are shaped, conditioned, and digitized at a 25 ns interval. The Phase-II Upgrade for the HL-LHC aims to enhance the system's resilience against higher radiation levels and out-of-time pileup. Under this upgrade, all calorimeter signals will be digitized and transmitted to off-detector systems for event reconstruction and forwarding to the Level-1 trigger at a 40 MHz rate. This capability will enable the development of more sophisticated trigger algorithms by providing the trigger system with higher-precision calorimeter data. The new hardware features state-of-the-art, radiation-hard electronics with redundant designs to prevent single points of failure, alongside multi-Gbps optical links for managing high data volumes and Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) to control logic for both on- and off-detector electronics. Furthermore, a hybrid demonstrator prototype module, incorporating the new calorimeter electronics while remaining compatible with the existing system, was installed in ATLAS in June 2019 to facilitate real-condition testing of the Phase-II system.

This paper presents adversarially robust streaming algorithms for central machine learning and algorithmic problems, including regression and clustering, as well as their broader forms like subspace embedding, low-rank approximation, and coreset construction. Focusing on regression and numerical linear algebra tasks, we adopt the row arrival streaming model. Our findings stem from a straightforward yet potent insight: many importance sampling-based algorithms inherently provide adversarial robustness, whereas the widely used sketching-based approaches in streaming literature are vulnerable to such attacks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the established merge-and-reduce paradigm in streaming is also resistant to adversarial manipulation. Given that this paradigm enables coreset construction, we derive robust algorithms for $k$-means, $k$-median, $k$-center, Bregman clustering, projective clustering, principal component analysis (PCA), and non-negative matrix factorization. To our knowledge, these represent the first adversarially robust solutions for these specific problems without necessitating new algorithmic implementations. Finally, empirical evaluations confirm the robustness of our methods against various adversarial attacks, highlighting that many common existing algorithms fail to maintain this property.

The literature has explored various Constraint Satisfaction Problem variants to model scenarios involving solution costs. While finding an optimal solution is generally NP-hard within these frameworks, the problem becomes solvable in polynomial time when restricted to instances where constraint interactions form (nearly-)acyclic graphs. This paper identifies broader classes of tractable instances by examining solution strategies that leverage hypergraph acyclicity and, more broadly, structural decomposition techniques like (hyper)tree decompositions.

In a recent publication, we introduced a broad geometric framework for defining initial data at big bang singularities, a concept valuable both independently and as a means to unify various findings in the literature. This paper provides partial support for that claim by recasting results regarding Bianchi class A orthogonal stiff solutions and $\mathbb{T}^{3}$-Gowdy symmetric vacuum solutions through the lens of our proposed general geometric notion of initial data on the big bang singularity.

Bipolar nanochannels, featuring alternating positively and negatively charged wall domains along their length, are recognized for rectifying current under an electric potential bias. Our findings indicate that incorporating charged nanoparticles can significantly enhance this rectification, increasing it by roughly an order of magnitude. We analyzed two distinct bipolar channel geometries, evaluating their behavior in resting states as well as under negative and positive bias conditions, utilizing a molecular-level model of the electrolyte solution. This substantial boost in current rectification is attributed to the intrinsic electric field generated by the charged nanoparticles within the channel. We determined that this phenomenon is highly dependent on the pore's geometry, its charge distribution, and the polarity of the nanoparticles' charge, thereby presenting novel prospects for designing engineered nanopore-membrane-nanoparticle systems for energy storage applications.

Object tracking in video sequences depends on capturing the spatial-temporal dynamics between objects. This paper introduces TransMOT, a method utilizing advanced graph transformers to efficiently model these interactions. By organizing object trajectories into sparse weighted graphs, TransMOT constructs spatial and temporal transformer encoder layers along with a spatial graph transformer decoder to handle numerous objects. Compared to conventional Transformers, TransMOT offers superior computational efficiency and higher tracking accuracy. To further enhance speed and performance, we introduce a cascade association framework designed to manage low-confidence detections and long-term occlusions, which are computationally intensive. Evaluated across several benchmarks—MOT15, MOT16, MOT17, and MOT20—the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art results on all datasets.

This study examines model-based approaches within multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). We define both dynamics and opponent sample complexities, performing a theoretical analysis of the upper bound for return discrepancy. To minimize this upper bound and achieve low sample complexity throughout the learning process, we introduce a novel decentralized model-based MARL framework called Adaptive Opponent-wise Rollout Policy Optimization (AORPO). Within AORPO, every agent constructs a multi-agent environment model comprising a dynamics model and several opponent models, then trains its policy using adaptive opponent-wise rollouts. Furthermore, we establish the theoretical convergence of AORPO under plausible assumptions. Empirical results on both cooperative and competitive tasks indicate that AORPO attains superior sample efficiency while maintaining comparable asymptotic performance relative to other MARL methods.

We demonstrate that the restriction map, which connects the subspace of regular points within the holonomy-perturbed traceless flat SU(2) moduli space of a tangle in a 3-manifold to the traceless flat moduli space of its boundary marked surface, constitutes a Lagrangian immersion. Central to our proof is the application of composition within the Weinstein category, alongside the observation that SU(2) holonomy perturbations in a cylinder result in Hamiltonian isotopies. Furthermore, we establish that the 2-sphere with four marked points, denoted as $(S^2,4)$, serves as its own traceless flat SU(2) moduli space.

We examine maps defined on the unit interval, characterized by a graph composed of two increasing segments and an extended injectivity property. These maps, denoted as $f_{\p}$, are determined by a quintuple $\p$ of real numbers subject to specific inequalities. When interpreted as circle maps, we demonstrate that $f_{\p}$ possesses a rotation number $\rho(f_{\p})$ and calculate this number as a function of $\p$ using Hecke-Mahler series. Consequently, we establish that $\rho(f_{\p})$ takes the form of a rational number whenever the elements of $\p$ are algebraic.
This paper posits that recommendation systems occupy a distinctive role in disseminating harmful and cruel conduct to individuals suffering from mental health conditions.

This research seeks to develop a theoretical framework for nonequilibrium processes in a Bose-Einstein condensate system linked to spontaneous symmetry breaking, employing Thermo Field Dynamics. We outline the most general expressions for a 4x4 transformation and an unperturbed Hamiltonian. Following the calculation of the 4x4 self-energy and the identification of its on-shell component, we apply a renormalization condition requiring the total on-shell self-energy to vanish. This constraint yields a sufficient set of independent equations to resolve all parameters within the unperturbed Hamiltonian, including the quantum transport equations governing normal and anomalous number distributions.

Current Deep Neural Network (DNN) testing often relies on Metamorphic Testing (MT), which typically involves mutating input images in a semantics-preserving manner to verify if DNN outputs remain consistent. However, we have discovered that DNNs may occasionally make predictions based on flawed reasoning—specifically, by relying on incorrect input components that coincidentally lead to the same output. Consequently, existing MT frameworks fail to detect these specific defects. Despite this, such erroneous decision-making processes are likely to cause a cascade of incorrect predictions when applied to diverse real-world images. This study seeks to reveal the prevalence of these hidden DNN defects, which stem from faulty decisions yet result in consistent predictions. To achieve this, we adapted and refined modern Explainable AI (XAI) methods to pinpoint visual concepts within input images that drive DNN predictions. Furthermore, we enhanced current MT-based testing frameworks to assess the consistency of the underlying DNN decisions across an input and its mutated versions. Our evaluation demonstrates that existing MT approaches overlook a significant number of defects arising from erroneous decisions. We validated our findings and clarified their nature through human evaluations. Additionally, by examining DNN decision-based metamorphic relations, we re-evaluated the efficacy of the transformation techniques proposed by prior MT frameworks. Finally, we synthesize key lessons from this research to offer valuable insights and guidance for future DNN testing efforts.

This paper investigates positive singular solutions for semilinear elliptic equations that include a first-order term and a singular nonlinearity. By employing a refined version of the Alexandrov-Serrin moving plane method and strategically selecting cutoff functions, we establish the symmetry and monotonicity characteristics of these solutions.

We report the inaugural systematic, broad-band X-ray investigation of super-Eddington accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs), utilizing simultaneous {\it NuSTAR} and {\it XMM-Newton} or {\it Swift}/XRT data for a sample of eight super-Eddington accreting AGN with Eddington ratios ranging from $1<\lambda_{\rm Edd}<426$. Our findings indicate that these super-Eddington AGN (SEAMBHs) exhibit a steep primary continuum slope, consistent with expectations for the super-Eddington regime and largely driven by relativistic reflection. The Iron K$\alpha$ emission lines in our sample display relativistic broadening, while the equivalent widths of their narrow components adhere to the 'X-ray Baldwin' effect, also referred to as the 'Iwasawa-Taniguchi' effect. We identified a statistically significant correlation between the photon index of the primary power-law and the Eddington ratio, aligning with previous research. Furthermore, consistent with super-Eddington characteristics, the median reflection fraction for our analyzed sources is approximately a factor of two higher than that of type\,1 AGN in the BASS sample. By estimating coronal temperatures for three sources—Mrk\,382 ($kT_e=7.8$\,keV), PG\,0026+129 ($kT_e=39$\,keV), and IRAS\,04416+1215 ($kT_e=3$\,keV)—we examined their placement on the compactness-temperature diagram. This analysis suggests that, similar to lower Eddington ratio AGN, the X-ray corona in super-Eddington AGN is regulated by pair production and annihilation.

Repeated assessments of biomarkers offer insights into survival hazards, yet these data are often collected intermittently and suffer from significant measurement error. Joint modeling of longitudinal and survival data provides a framework to link error-prone, irregularly measured biomarkers with survival risks. However, most existing joint models rely on Gaussian assumptions, rendering them vulnerable to outliers. This study investigates various robust modeling approaches to mitigate this vulnerability. Recognizing that outliers in medical data may appear with varying frequencies over time, we introduce a novel model featuring time-varying robustness. Using both simulation studies and analyses of two real-world datasets, this research underscores the necessity of accounting for longitudinal outliers in joint modeling and demonstrates the bias and inefficiency resulting from failing to accurately estimate the degrees-of-freedom parameter. All methods presented in this work can be implemented using the R package `robjm`.

We introduce t-SR, a temporally extended adaptation of the successor representation that models the dynamics of long-duration actions by building successor representations based on repeated primitive actions. Unlike approaches that learn a top-down hierarchy of task structures, t-SR constructs a bottom-up composition of coupled actions and their repetitions. This approach reduces the frequency of control decisions without necessitating a hierarchical policy. Consequently, t-SR directly accounts for the time horizon of temporally extended action sequences without relying on predefined or domain-specific options. We demonstrate that in environments featuring dynamic reward structures, t-SR effectively combines the flexibility of the successor representation with the abstraction capabilities of temporally extended actions. In a series of sparsely rewarded gridworld tasks, t-SR achieves optimal adaptation of learned policies significantly faster than comparable model-free, value-based reinforcement learning methods. Furthermore, we show that solving these tasks with t-SR requires sampling the learned policy consistently less often than when using non-temporally extended policies.

The minimal seesaw extension of the Standard Model necessitates two electroweak singlet fermions to account for neutrino oscillation parameters at tree level. This study examines a next-to-minimal extension where light neutrino masses arise radiatively from two electroweak fermions: one singlet and one SU(2) triplet. These fermions must be odd under a parity symmetry, and their mixing produces a stable weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter candidate. For masses within the GeV-TeV range, this model yields the correct relic density and predicts observable signals in nuclear recoil direct detection experiments. Additionally, the gauge interactions of the fermion triplet component render it potentially detectable at current and near-future collider experiments.

We present the vanishing adsorption criterion for contact discontinuities and apply it to the Glimm-Isaacson model of chemical flooding in petroleum reservoirs. We demonstrate that this physically derived criterion validates the admissibility conditions previously established by Keyfitz-Kranzer, Isaacson-Temple, and de Souza-Marchesin for scenarios where the fractional flow function varies monotonically with chemical concentration. Furthermore, we show that the adsorption criterion identifies the undercompressive contact discontinuities necessary to resolve the general Riemann problem in an example model featuring non-monotone dependence.

This paper constructs integrals of motion within a para-Bose framework for a general time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian that commutes with the reflection operator. Within this context, we derive generalizations of coherent states (CS) and squeezed vacuum states (SVS) using the Wigner parameter. Additionally, we demonstrate a completeness relation for these generalized SVS based on the Wigner parameter. Regarding probability transitions, our findings indicate that the displacement parameter facilitates access to odd states, whereas the Wigner parameter governs the distribution's dispersion. By requiring the vacuum state to possess even parity, we establish that the Wigner parameter is quantized. Applying these general results to a time-independent para-Bose oscillator, we observe that the mean values of position and momentum exhibit oscillatory behavior akin to the simple harmonic oscillator, while the standard deviation incorporates corrections dependent on the squeeze, displacement, and Wigner parameters.

An accompanying article (arXiv:2112.05472) introduced and recommended a gauge-invariant framework for calculating bubble nucleation rates at finite temperatures with radiative barriers for use in model-building and phenomenology. This paper elaborates on that computation using the Abelian Higgs Model as a demonstration. We then reformulate the method within the dimensionally-reduced high-temperature effective field theory, enabling the inclusion of multiple higher-order thermal resummations and providing a clear definition of the approach's validity limits. This methodology facilitates robust perturbative analyses of bubble nucleation during potential first-order cosmic phase transitions, with significant implications for electroweak baryogenesis and the generation of a stochastic gravitational wave background. Additionally, it establishes a reliable comparison between perturbative and non-perturbative computational results.

Subdwarf B (sdB) stars are vital to understanding stellar evolution, asteroseismology, and the far-ultraviolet output of early-type galaxies, making them a frequent subject of theoretical and observational research. Although models predict the existence of sdB binaries with neutron star (NS) companions in the Galaxy, none have been observed to date, representing a significant unresolved puzzle. While a previous study (Paper I) modeled the formation of sdB+NS systems from main-sequence (MS) and NS progenitors, the origin of these initial MS+NS binaries remained unexplained. This work systematically traces the formation of sdB+NS binaries from their zero-age main-sequence progenitors to fill that gap. Our goal is to determine the statistical population characteristics of these systems and offer direction for future observations. Methodologically, we utilized Hurley's Binary Star Evolution (BSE) code to simulate $10^7$ primordial binaries until the NS companions in MS, Hertzsprung gap (HG), and Giant Branch (GB) systems filled their Roche lobes. These evolved binaries were then integrated into the Paper I model grid to derive sdB+NS population properties. We analyzed two distinct neutron star natal kick prescriptions and varied common-envelope ejection efficiencies to assess their impact on the outcomes. The results indicate that the majority of sdB+NS binaries reside in the Galactic disk with low radial velocity semi-amplitudes. However, systems with large radial velocity semi-amplitudes are predicted to be potent gravitational wave sources, potentially detectable by LISA in the future.

Ensuring secure data transmission is a critical challenge in wireless relay networks, making physical layer security a promising solution. This paper examines a cooperative network comprising a source, a destination, an eavesdropper, and multiple relay nodes, where the source selects specific relays to optimize security performance. However, relays may be incentivized to misrepresent their private channel information to increase selection probability and maximize their payoff. To mitigate this dishonesty, we introduce two mechanisms: one based on the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) auction and another on the Arrow-d'Aspremont-Gerard-Varet (AGV) auction. By designing distinct transfer payment functions for the selected relays, we demonstrate that each relay achieves its maximum expected payoff by truthfully disclosing its channel state, thereby enabling the network to reach optimal secrecy rates. Following a comparative analysis of both mechanisms, we prove that the AGV approach satisfies all fundamental qualifications for the system, including incentive compatibility, individual rationality, and budget balance. Furthermore, we determine the optimal number of relays the source should employ. Simulation results confirm the efficiency and fairness of both mechanisms, validating our findings.

Current randomized methods require a preliminary estimate of the tubal rank to perform tensor singular value decomposition. This study introduces a novel randomized algorithm with fixed precision that, given a third-order tensor and a specified error tolerance, automatically determines both the tubal rank and the corresponding low-rank approximation. Leveraging random projection techniques alongside power iteration to enhance accuracy, the proposed method was evaluated through simulations on both synthetic and real-world datasets to demonstrate its efficiency and performance.

In hot accretion flows, the collisional mean free path of charged particles often exceeds the characteristic length scale of the flow, leading to gas pressure anisotropy relative to magnetic field lines. Under these conditions, resistive dissipation plays a crucial role. This study examines the dynamics of resistive hot accretion flows incorporating anisotropic pressure by deriving self-similar solutions where flow variables depend solely on radius. Our findings demonstrate that radial and rotational velocities, as well as sound speed, increase substantially with greater anisotropic pressure strength. Furthermore, when resistive dissipation is included, the enhancements in infall velocity and sound speed become even more pronounced, with these variations also dependent on magnetic field strength. Specifically, when the anisotropic pressure strength is 0.1, resistive heating accounts for approximately 10% of the heating generated by the work done by anisotropic pressure; this proportion rises as the anisotropic pressure strength decreases. Consequently, the resulting rise in disk temperature can heat and accelerate electrons, offering a potential explanation for phenomena such as flares in the Galactic Center's Sgr A*.

Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) offer a rapid solution for delivering goods and mobile services; however, they deplete their energy reserves quickly during transit, and even solar-powered units require significant time to recharge en route. To mitigate this, current research primarily focuses on path planning supported by dedicated system vehicles for charging. Nevertheless, in scenarios involving emergencies or rural regions where such vehicles are unavailable, leveraging public trucks presents a more viable and economical alternative. This study investigates how a single UAV can reduce its flight distance—and consequently minimize travel time—by utilizing public trucks. We present the first theoretical analysis of online algorithms for this problem, ensuring guaranteed worst-case performance. Initially, we address the offline scenario with full advance knowledge of truck schedules by transforming the problem into a graph that respects both temporal and power constraints, yielding a shortest-path algorithm for the optimal solution. Subsequently, we examine the online setting, where truck availability is revealed in real-time with a notification lead time of $\Delta t$. We establish a theoretical lower bound as a benchmark for online algorithms. We introduce two approaches: "MyopicHitching," which greedily selects truck rides, and an enhanced "$\Delta t$-Adaptive" algorithm that allows for strategic waiting. Our analysis demonstrates that the $\Delta t$-Adaptive algorithm is asymptotically optimal, as its performance ratio converges to the established lower bound as $\Delta t$ increases.

This contribution provides a concise overview of an invited talk on observational supernova science conducted at the Nordic Optical Telescope at Stockholm University over the last 25 years, along with future outlooks.

The $(g-2)_\mu$ anomaly suggests that second-generation leptons must possess interactions beyond the Standard Model. Given the high flux of $
u_\mu$ and $ ar{
u}_\mu$ observed in forward experiments like FASER$
u$ and SND@LHC, these facilities are ideal for probing such new interactions. This paper presents a model where second-generation left-handed leptons interact with a new right-handed neutrino, $N$, and a novel Higgs doublet that also couples to quarks. In this framework, high-energy $
u_\mu$ scattering off nuclei can generate $N$. We examine how forward experiments can test this scenario by searching for the production vertex of $N$ followed by its displaced decay vertex. Observing even a single event could signal the potential for detecting the new Higgs doublet at the LHC. Furthermore, we explore the possibility of resolving the $(g-2)_\mu$ anomaly by introducing additional generations of $N$, which would result in chain decays producing multiple leptons with distinct signatures detectable at forward experiments, as well as at the CMS and ATLAS detectors. Finally, we demonstrate that incorporating a new light singlet scalar mixed with the neutral component of the new Higgs doublet (the 2HDM+$S$ model) can significantly enhance the statistical power of the data sample.

Investigating physics beyond the Standard Model (SM) is well-served by the decay of Higgs boson-like particles into multileptons, a final state characterized by the high precision of our SM knowledge, which allows simulations to directly estimate backgrounds. While existing searches often restrict themselves to specific models with a single free parameter to streamline analysis, this paper examines recent machine learning proposals for model-agnostic searches within the multilepton channel. These methods enable simultaneous exploration of numerous models, including those without dedicated Large Hadron Collider searches. Our findings indicate that machine learning provides extensive coverage across the parameter space beyond current search sensitivities, with a performance reduction relative to dedicated searches of only approximately one order of magnitude.

This article investigates quantized matrix algebras, specifically at a root of unity. It provides a comprehensive classification of simple modules for rank 2 quantized matrix algebras and introduces a class of finite-dimensional indecomposable modules.

We introduce and validate the task of generating natural language summaries describing a robotic agent's actions within a virtual setting. We outline the significance of this challenge, identify its complexities, and explore potential solutions. To foster further research, we demonstrate how a widely used dataset originally designed for instruction following—pairing robot actions with natural language descriptions—can be adapted to train models for robot action summarization. We propose and evaluate multiple learning approaches for creating these summaries, utilizing either egocentric video footage of the robot or intermediate textual representations from an automatic planner. Finally, we offer both quantitative and qualitative assessments of our findings, establishing a baseline for future investigations.

The element distinctness problem seeks to identify if a sequence $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$ of $N$ elements includes any two identical values, a challenge for which Ambainis developed an optimal quantum solution. This approach involves first reducing the general problem to a "promised" variant where $x$ is guaranteed to have at most one colliding pair, followed by constructing an algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ that uses $O(N^{2/3})$ queries via quantum walk search. Although $\mathcal{A}$ is probabilistic and prone to error, this work presents an exact quantum algorithm for the promise problem that ensures zero error while maintaining the $O(N^{2/3})$ query complexity and proving its optimality. Methodologically, we adapt the quantum walk search operator on quasi-Johnson graphs to incorporate arbitrary phases and apply Jordan's lemma to transform the operator into a generalized Grover's operator. This facilitates the application of the recently introduced fixed-axis-rotation (FXR) method for exact quantum search, thereby achieving a 100% success rate.

This study examines a semilinear wave equation featuring time-dependent damping, expressed as $-\frac{1}{{(1+t)}^{\beta}}\Delta u_t$, alongside a nonlinearity of $|u|^p$. Employing the test function method, we demonstrate how the parameter $\beta$ affects blow-up outcomes, contingent upon specific conditions regarding the initial data and the exponent $p$. Additionally, we analyze the local existence of mild solutions within the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ over a finite time interval.

This research investigates supersymmetric configurations within four-dimensional $N=6$ gauged supergravity featuring an $SO(6)$ gauge group. We identify a singular $N=6$ supersymmetric $AdS_4$ vacuum possessing $SO(6)$ symmetry, which corresponds holographically to a three-dimensional $N=6$ superconformal field theory (SCFT). Our analysis reveals several domain walls connecting this vacuum to infrared singular geometries characterized by $SO(2)\times SO(4)$, $U(3)$, $SO(3)$, and $SO(2)\times SO(2)\times SO(2)$ symmetries. Specifically, the $SO(3)$ sector supports both $N=6$ and $N=2$ solutions, contingent on the presence of pseudoscalars, whereas all other identified solutions maintain $N=6$ supersymmetry. These configurations represent renormalization group (RG) flows from the $N=6$ SCFT to non-conformal field theories induced by mass deformations; notably, the $SO(2)\times SO(4)$ solution aligns with established mass deformations of the dual SCFT. Furthermore, we present a supersymmetric Janus solution with $SO(2)\times SO(4)$ symmetry, modeling two-dimensional conformal defects within the $N=6$ SCFT that preserve $N=(4,2)$ supersymmetry. Additionally, we discover an $N=2$ supersymmetric $AdS_2\times H^2$ solution with $SO(2)\times SO(4)$ symmetry, linked by a domain wall to the $AdS_4$ vacuum. This setup describes an $AdS_4$ black hole carrying magnetic charge and is dual to a twisted compactification of the $N=6$ SCFT on a hyperbolic space $H^2$. Finally, we provide a domain wall interpolating between a locally supersymmetric $AdS_4$ and a curved domain wall with $SO(2)\times SO(2)\times SO(2)$ symmetry, which corresponds to an RG flow across dimensions from the $N=6$ SCFT down to a supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

This study addresses a stochastic system identification task: estimating the drift field of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) driven by Lévy $\alpha$-stable noise using time series data. For $\alpha$ values within $[1,2)$, the heavy-tailed nature of the noise creates computational challenges for approaches relying on physical space transition densities or likelihoods. To overcome this, we introduce a Fourier space method centered on calculating time-dependent characteristic functions, which are the Fourier transforms of time-evolving densities. By representing the unknown drift field as a Fourier series, we define a loss function based on the squared error between empirical and predicted characteristic functions. This loss is minimized using gradients derived from the adjoint method. Our results, tested across various one- and two-dimensional scenarios, show that the proposed method effectively learns drift fields that align qualitatively and/or quantitatively with ground truth data.

Optimizing for Top-1 ImageNet accuracy often results in excessively large networks that are impractical for inference. Although Binary Neural Networks (BNNs) offer significant computational savings, current models suffer from poor accuracy. To address this, we introduce PokeConv, a binary convolutional block that enhances BNN performance through techniques like multi-path residual connections and optimized activation functions. We apply this block to ResNet-50, specifically addressing the difficulty of binarizing its initial convolutional layer, creating the PokeBNN network family. These methods are designed to simultaneously improve top-1 accuracy and reduce computational cost. To facilitate joint optimization of these factors, we define Arithmetic Computation Effort (ACE), a cost metric inspired by hardware and energy constraints for quantized and binarized networks. We also highlight the importance of tuning an under-explored hyper-parameter related to binarization gradient approximation. Our approach establishes a new state-of-the-art (SOTA) across top-1 accuracy, CPU64 cost, ACE, and network size. While the previous SOTA, ReActNet-Adam, achieved 70.5% top-1 accuracy with an ACE of 7.9, a compact PokeBNN variant matches this accuracy with an ACE of 2.6 (over 3x cost reduction), and a larger variant reaches 75.6% top-1 accuracy with an ACE of 7.8 (over 5% accuracy gain without cost increase). Implementation details and reproduction scripts for PokeBNN in JAX/Flax are available in the AQT repository: https://github.com/google/aqt.

The fully implicit approach is the standard technique for addressing black-oil issues in reservoir simulation, though it demands repeated linearization of large nonlinear systems and often results in ill-conditioned linear equations. To mitigate computational costs, we propose a strategy built on two core concepts: (\textit{i}) a sequential formulation that separates flow and transport into distinct subproblems, and (\textit{ii}) a highly efficient Gauss--Seidel solver for transport. This solver leverages intercell fluxes to reorder grid cells based on their upstream neighbors and groups cells with mutual dependencies arising from counter-current flow into local clusters. These cells and clusters are then solved sequentially, progressing from inflow to downstream regions, as each new element relies solely on previously computed upstream neighbors. This approach ensures optimal localization and control over the nonlinear solution process. While this method has proven effective for real-field scenarios using standard first-order finite volume discretization, we now extend the concept to first-order discontinuous Galerkin (dG) methods on fully unstructured grids. Furthermore, we validate the reordering concept by applying it to the complete Norne oil field simulation model using a prototype version of the open-source OPM Flow simulator.

This paper presents a flexible, modular framework for developing multimodal interactive agents. The system functions via an event bus that sequentially broadcasts signals and interpretations, allowing various sensors and interpretation modules to be integrated by specifying their input and output topics, thereby establishing a logical workflow for subsequent processing. The authors detail a wide array of components currently developed and integrated into diverse interactive agents. Furthermore, the paper outlines how interactions are captured as both multimodal data and within an episodic Knowledge Graph. By analyzing this recorded interaction data, researchers can evaluate and compare different agents and their constituent components.

This study examines a steady-state convection-diffusion problem characterized by a diffusion coefficient of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ within a thin, three-dimensional graph-like junction. This junction comprises slender cylinders linked by a central node with a diameter of $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$, where $\varepsilon$ denotes a small parameter. By employing multiscale analysis, the authors construct and validate an asymptotic expansion for the solution. Furthermore, they establish asymptotic estimates in both the $H^1$ Sobolev norm and the uniform norm, demonstrating that the discrepancy between the exact solution and the proposed approximations achieves a predetermined level of accuracy relative to the power of $\varepsilon$.

Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) represent a transformative technology for sixth-generation (6G) networks due to their capacity to manipulate wireless propagation environments. However, as frequency-selective devices, RIS units can only effectively shape signals within specific frequency bands. This characteristic complicates base station (BS)-RIS-user association in cellular networks, particularly when adjacent base stations operate on different frequency bands. Addressing these frequency-selective constraints, this paper proposes a framework to jointly optimize BS-RIS-user association, active beamforming at base stations, and passive beamforming at RIS units, aiming to maximize the sum-rate of RIS-assisted cellular networks. The approach utilizes the $l_0$-norm to efficiently integrate association decisions with beamforming designs. Subsequently, fractional programming (FP) and block coordinate descent (BCD) techniques are employed to handle logarithmic and fractional components, decoupling the complex joint optimization problem into manageable sub-problems. To solve these sub-problems iteratively, efficient algorithms combining $l_0$-norm approximation, majorization-minimization (MM), and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) are developed. Extensive simulations demonstrate the critical role of optimizing BS-RIS-user association in such networks and validate the efficacy of the proposed joint association and beamforming algorithm.

The influence of stellar multiplicity on planetary system formation and evolution is intricate. Demographic studies combining high-resolution imaging and radial velocity data suggest that close binaries significantly hinder planet formation, whereas wide companions have minimal impact. However, limitations in the magnitude and distance reach of these methods leave vast ranges of mass ratios and separations underexplored. We utilize the Gaia Mission's Early Data Release 3 (EDR3), which provides radial velocity measurements for over 6.5 million targets, to investigate binary companions within a statistical framework named "paired."
